title: Are a square piece and a triangle piece the same size?
description: A whole chikki of 24 squares is cut into six equal parts in two different ways, once into square pieces and once into triangle pieces. Counting squares shows both kinds cover the same amount. Keeko's doubt, that the square piece is bigger, is broken.
teaching_notes: One idea: a fraction of a whole depends on how much the piece covers, not on its shape. Watch for students who think a thin, pointed piece is smaller than a square one.

source: By dividing the whole chikki into 6 equal parts in different ways, we get 1/6 chikki pieces of different shapes. Are they of the same size?
video_script.why: The child sees that a fraction of a whole is about how much a piece covers, not what shape it has, by counting small squares in two one sixth pieces.
video_script.substitution: Measure each piece in the small squares of the chikki and compare the counts, not the shapes.
video_script.anchor: A whole chikki of 24 small squares cut into six equal parts in two different ways, with square pieces and with triangle pieces
video_script.wrong_answer: the square piece is bigger because the triangle looks thin and pointy
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says the square piece is bigger because the triangle looks thin and pointy. Two triangles fill one strip and two square pieces fill the same strip, so the bubble is struck.
video_script.payoff_line: Both pieces are one sixth of the chikki

final_answer.value: yes, the same size; each is 1/6 chikki (4 small squares)
final_answer.spoken: both pieces are one sixth of the chikki, so they are the same size

never_show: the triangle piece as smaller than the square piece
maths_rules: whole chikki: 6 across, 4 down, 6 x 4 = 24 small squares
6 equal parts of 24 squares: 24 / 6 = 4 squares each, so each part is 1/6
way one: 6 square pieces of 2 by 2 squares, 2 x 2 = 4 squares each
way two: 3 strips of 2 across and 4 down (8 squares each), each strip cut corner to corner into 2 equal triangles of 8 / 2 = 4 squares each
one strip of 8 squares = 2 square pieces = 2 triangles, so one triangle covers as much as one square piece
slip: shape does not set the fraction; equal coverage does
video_script.design: One idea: the same amount covered means the same fraction, whatever the shape. Assumes the broken chikki question on fourths. Wrong idea: a thin shape is a smaller share. The two cut chikkis stay on the board to the end.

narration: <bookmark mark='divide'/>Step one, share the twenty four squares into six equal parts. Twenty four divided by six is four, so each part covers four squares.

narration: <bookmark mark='square'/>Step two, count the square piece. It is two squares across and two down, so it covers four squares.

marks.strip: a strip of two across and four down is cut corner to corner into two triangles
marks.same: one triangle and one square piece are laid side by side and both cover four squares

narration: <bookmark mark='strip'/>Step three, count the triangle in the same way as the example in your book. A triangle is half of a strip of eight squares.
<bookmark mark='same'/>Eight divided by two is four, so the triangle covers four squares too.

beats.on_screen: Answer: yes, the same size; each piece is 1/6 chikki (4 small squares)
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Both pieces are one sixth of the chikki. They are the same size, and only their shapes are different.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the square piece is bigger because the triangle looks thin and pointy.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But two triangles fill one strip, and two square pieces fill the same strip.
<bookmark mark='shape'/>What matters is how much a piece covers, not how it looks.
